question: Java 17 reachability model: one object O has two strong local root references a and b. No other references exist. Set a=null while b still refers to O. Is O eligible for garbage collection solely because of this assignment?

options.A: Yes; clearing any one reference immediately makes an object unreachable
options.B: It must be collected immediately before the next statement
options.C: No; O remains strongly reachable through b
options.D: Yes; an object can have only one GC root

explanation: Reachability is determined from all strong roots, not one chosen variable. b still provides a root-to-object path. Neither eligibility nor a particular collection time follows from setting only a to null.

question: Java 17 reachability model: objects A and B reference each other. Their only strong root references are variables a and b, which are both set to null. There are no finalization, reference-queue, or native-root complications, and no collector runs during the assignments. How many of these two objects are now unreachable and eligible for collection?

options.C: They remain reachable solely because the cycle exists

explanation: An isolated cycle does not keep itself reachable from a GC root. After both external roots disappear, neither object has a root path, so both are eligible; this does not promise when a collector will run.

question: Java 17 reachability model: four objects A,B,C,D exist, with strong roots r->A and s->D. Edges are A->B, B->C, C->B, and D->C. No other roots/references exist, and no collector runs during the steps. First set r=null, then s=null. What is the pair (newly unreachable objects after the first step, total unreachable original objects after both steps)?
explanation: After r is cleared, A alone is unreachable: s reaches D,C,B despite the B-C cycle. After s is also cleared, no root reaches any original object, so all four are unreachable. The counts concern reachability, not a promised collection schedule.
